headline: UK Household Energy Bills Projected to Rise 26% in 2027
summary: UK energy bills are expected to increase by 26% in January 2027, reaching their highest level since 2023. The rise is attributed to elevated wholesale gas and electricity prices driven by the ongoing conflict involving Iran.
why: Energy price caps set by the regulator Ofgem directly influence household utility costs in the UK, impacting consumer disposable income and national inflation metrics.

impacts.name: Utilities
impacts.why: Higher price caps allow energy providers to pass increased wholesale costs to consumers.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The projected increase in energy price caps directly raises the cost of living for UK households, which can dampen consumer spending and influence central bank interest rate policy.
